monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with a notable increase in Zone 4 time and faster average pace, but at the cost of reduced volume and lower aerobic TE — suggesting a recent emphasis on quality over quantity.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 time jumped from 15% last month to 35% this month — the largest proportional shift across all HR zones, indicating a sharp pivot toward threshold and hard efforts.

goal_tracker.message: You need 39.6 more km across 7 remaining sessions — averaging ~5.7 km per session — to match last month's volume. Given your recent 10.0 km long run and strong aerobic TE (4.0), 3–4 runs of 5–7 km at Zone 2–3 HR would be realistic and sustainable.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite lower cadence
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.46 to 13.9 m/beat while cadence dropped from 151 to 148 spm — driven by longer stride length (72.2 → 75.7 cm) and reduced ground contact time (312 → 305 ms) in your 10.0 km run, suggesting improved neuromuscular coordination at sustained effort.

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 4 at expense of foundational zones
insights.body: Zone 4 now accounts for 35% of total HR time (up from 15%), while Z1+Z2 dropped from 53% to 28% — meaning nearly 3/4 of your HR distribution is now in or above lactate threshold, risking under-recovery and limiting aerobic base development.

insights.title: Stride length increased, but vertical oscillation remains stable
insights.body: Stride length rose from 72.2 cm (6.5 km run, Jun 28) to 75.7 cm (10.0 km run, Jul 5), yet vertical oscillation stayed tightly clustered between 7.6–8.5 cm — indicating efficient power transfer without excessive bounce, likely supporting your pace improvement.

insights.title: High-intensity density without recovery buffer
insights.body: Your four July runs include three with aerobic TE ≥3.0 (including a 4.0 on the 10.0 km), yet only one very short recovery run (0.9 km, TE=2.0); no run this month had TE <2.0 — suggesting insufficient low-stress recovery stimulus.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on your next easy day, focusing on cadence ≥150 spm and stride length ≥74 cm
recommendations.reason: Your Z1+Z2 time has fallen to just 28% this month, and your lowest HR in recent runs was 129 bpm (Jul 08, 4.0 km) — this session will rebuild aerobic capacity while reinforcing form metrics that support efficiency.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming mid-week run with a 3 × 8-min Zone 3 intervals (HR 150–158 bpm) with 90-sec walk recovery
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 3 time dropped from 31% (Jun) to 20% (Jul), and your best pace (475 sec/km = 7:55/km) occurred during a Zone 4-heavy week — structured Zone 3 work bridges endurance and threshold adaptation without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Add 2-min barefoot strides (on grass) post-run twice this week, emphasizing light footstrike and 160+ spm
recommendations.reason: Cadence declined from 151 to 148 spm this month, and your slowest recent run (Jul 08, 8:32/km) showed lowest cadence (136 spm) — neuromuscular priming will help maintain turnover under fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Rebalance intensity distribution by restoring Z2 volume, stabilizing cadence, and reinforcing efficient stride mechanics — all while preserving recent gains in threshold capability.
suggested_sessions: 4.5 km progressive run: start Z2, finish last 1.5 km at Z3 (HR 148–155 bpm)
